findings.quote: Finding d₁ correctly as 8g but computing d₂ from the shortcut d₂ = t₂² − t₁² = 144 − 16 = 128, forgetting the ½g factor, giving 128g/8g = 16.
findings.note: The stated cause contradicts its own arithmetic: if the whole ½g factor is dropped, d₂ = 128 while d₁ = 8g, and dropping ½g in both lines gives 128/16 = 8, the correct answer. Only dropping the factor ½ while keeping g gives the printed 128g/8g = 16.
findings.fix: Finding d₁ correctly as 8g but writing d₂ = g(t₂² − t₁²) = g(144 − 16) = 128g, forgetting the factor ½, giving 128g/8g = 16.

notes: Solved independently: d₁ = ½g(4)² = 8g, d₂ = ½g(144 − 16) = 64g, ratio 8. Checked every entry numerically: 8/4 = 2 lands on option 2. A brute-force search over the times, their squares and the two distances found no route to option 4 (12) other than 4 + 8, so the entry describing 12 as the summed time is honest and needs no distractor flag. Steps and approach are correct as printed.
